help.intro: From twenty-one upwards German says the numbers backwards from an English point of view: the unit first, then und, then the ten, all as one word — einundzwanzig is 'one-and-twenty'. Once you accept that order, everything to a hundred follows one pattern, and the tens themselves are the units with -zig on the end (vierzig, fünfzig, achtzig, neunzig) with the same two trims as before — sechzig, siebzig — and one odd one, dreißig, spelt with ß. Two details are worth getting right from the start: it is ein before und (einundzwanzig, never einsundzwanzig), and hundert can be said with or without ein.

tips.title: Unit + und + ten, one word
tips.text: 21 einundzwanzig, 34 vierunddreißig, 58 achtundfünfzig, 99 neunundneunzig. Read the digits right to left.

examples.de: Meine Mutter ist achtundvierzig.
examples.en: My mother is forty-eight.

examples.de: Das kostet dreiundzwanzig Euro.
examples.en: That costs twenty-three euros.

tips.trap: English says twenty-one; German says one-and-twenty. When you *hear* a number, the second half is the big part.

check.q: Das kostet ____ Euro. (36)
check.why: Unit first, then und, then the ten, as one word: sechs-und-dreißig. dreiundsechzig is 63.

visual.caption: Twenty-one is said one-and-twenty, and written as one word.

tips.title: The tens
tips.text: zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig, neunzig, (ein)hundert. Note dreißig with ß, and the trimmed sechzig and siebzig.

examples.de: Er ist dreißig. Sie ist sechzig.
examples.en: He is thirty. She is sixty.

examples.de: hundert Euro / einhundert Euro
examples.en: a hundred euros — both are correct

check.q: Mein Opa ist ____. (70)
check.why: The tens add -zig, and sieben is trimmed: siebzig. siebzehn is 17.

rows.note: sechs and sieben lose a piece, as in the teens.

tips.title: ein, not eins, before und
tips.text: The s of eins disappears inside a number: einundzwanzig, einunddreißig, einundvierzig.

examples.de: einundzwanzig, einunddreißig
Mein Vater ist einundfünfzig.
examples.en: My father is fifty-one.

check.q: Meine Tante ist ____. (41)
check.why: Inside a number eins loses its s: ein + und + vierzig = einundvierzig.

tips.title: Say it, then flip it
tips.text: When writing a heard number, say the German aloud, then write the *second* half first: 'sieben-und-vierzig' → 4, then 7 → 47.

examples.de: siebenundvierzig → 47
examples.en: 'seven and forty' → 47

examples.de: achtundsechzig → 68
examples.en: 'eight and sixty' → 68

check.q: You hear neunundsiebzig. Which number do you write?
check.why: The second half is the ten: siebzig → 7, then neun → 9, so 79.

remember: Backwards is forwards: the small number is said first.
-zig is the tens; dreißig is the only one spelt with ß.

context.de: Wie alt sind deine Eltern? – Mein Vater ist vierundfünfzig und meine Mutter ist einundfünfzig. Meine Oma ist schon achtundsiebzig! – Und was kostet die Jacke? – Neunundneunzig Euro. Zu teuer!
context.en: How old are your parents? – My father is fifty-four and my mother is fifty-one. My grandma is already seventy-eight! – And what does the jacket cost? – Ninety-nine euros. Too expensive!

mistakes.why: Unit first, then und, then the ten.
eins loses its s inside a number.
dreißig takes ß; sechzig is trimmed.

help.hook: German says twenty-one as 'one-and-twenty' — flip that one habit and every number up to a hundred is yours.

help.intro: Colours are the first adjectives you use to describe things, and at first you use them in the easy position: after the verb sein, where they never change — Das Auto ist rot. Die Blume ist gelb. (Before a noun an adjective takes an ending — ein rotes Auto — but that comes later in the course; for now you only need to recognise it.) You need eleven basic colours, and three of them are loanwords that never take any ending even later: rosa, lila and orange. This quiz gives you a clue and asks for the colour; the clues also quietly teach you nouns like Himmel, Gras and Sonne.

tips.title: After sein, colours don't change
tips.text: Das Auto ist rot. Die Autos sind rot. Der Himmel ist blau. Whatever the noun, the colour stays in its base form after ist / sind.

examples.de: Die Banane ist gelb.
examples.en: The banana is yellow.

examples.de: Meine Katze ist schwarz und weiß.
examples.en: My cat is black and white.

check.q: Die Tomaten sind ____.
check.why: After sein (ist / sind) the colour stays in its base form, whatever the noun: Die Tomaten sind rot.

tips.title: Before a noun it takes an ending — for later
tips.text: ein rotes Auto, eine gelbe Banane, der blaue Himmel. The endings come later in the course; for now just notice them when you read.

examples.de: Ich habe ein blaues Auto.
examples.en: I have a blue car.

examples.de: Das rote Auto ist neu.
examples.en: The red car is new.

tips.trap: English adjectives never change. Don't try to add endings yet; but don't be surprised to see them.

check.q: Which phrase shows a colour with an ending?
check.why: Before a noun the colour takes an ending (grün → grünes). After ist it stays plain.

tips.title: rosa and lila never change at all
tips.text: These two are borrowed and take no ending ever: ein rosa Kleid, die lila Blumen. orange is different: standard German does inflect it — ein oranges T-Shirt, der orange Pullover — though it is often left uninflected in speech.

examples.de: Sie trägt ein rosa Kleid.
examples.en: She is wearing a pink dress.

examples.de: Ich mag die lila Blumen.
examples.en: I like the purple flowers.

check.q: Ich kaufe ein ____ T-Shirt.
check.why: lila and rosa are borrowed colours and never take an ending, even before a noun.

tips.title: hell- and dunkel-
tips.text: Light and dark are prefixes glued to the colour: hellblau (light blue), dunkelgrün (dark green). bunt means many-coloured.

examples.de: Der Himmel ist hellblau. Der Wald ist dunkelgrün.
examples.en: The sky is light blue. The forest is dark green.

examples.de: Mein Pullover ist dunkelblau.
examples.en: My jumper is dark blue.

check.q: How do you say light blue?
check.why: hell- (light) and dunkel- (dark) are glued to the front of the colour: hellblau, dunkelblau.

remember: Blut is rot, Himmel is blau, Gras is grün, Sonne is gelb — the clues in this quiz are the mnemonic.
Three foreigners never change: rosa, lila, orange.

context.de: Mein Zimmer ist bunt: Die Wand ist gelb, der Teppich ist blau und die Lampe ist rot. Mein Stuhl ist schwarz. Und mein Lieblingskleid? Es ist rosa, natürlich!
context.en: My room is colourful: the wall is yellow, the carpet is blue and the lamp is red. My chair is black. And my favourite dress? It's pink, of course!

mistakes.why: After sein the adjective takes no ending.
rosa, lila and orange never take endings.
Same rule: base form after ist.

help.hook: Put a colour after ist and it never changes — Das Auto ist rot — the easiest adjectives you will ever learn.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Blut und Erdbeeren ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of blood and strawberries is ____ (red).
sentences.why: rot is 'red' — the two words are old cousins; hear it in 'rouge' too.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe vom Himmel ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of the sky is ____ (blue).
sentences.why: blau is 'blue' — nearly the same word, said with an ow sound.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Gras und Blättern ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of grass and leaves is ____ (green).
sentences.why: grün is 'green' — same family as grow and grass; the ü says ee with rounded lips.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von der Sonne und Bananen ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of the sun and bananas is ____ (yellow).
sentences.why: gelb is 'yellow' — both grew from the same old word; think of gold.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von der Nacht ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of the night is ____ (black).
sentences.why: schwarz is 'black' — the odd one out; English kept it in 'swarthy'.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Schnee und Milch ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of snow and milk is ____ (white).
sentences.why: weiß is 'white' — w and a sharp s (ß); same root as 'white'.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von einer Orange und Karotten ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of an orange and carrots is ____ (orange).
sentences.why: orange is the same word as in English — fruit and colour alike.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Schokolade und Holz ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of chocolate and wood is ____ (brown).
sentences.why: braun is 'brown' — the same word with German spelling, au = ow.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von einem Elefanten und Wolken ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of an elephant and clouds is ____ (grey).
sentences.why: grau is 'grey' — same root; au = ow, as in braun and blau.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von einem Flamingo ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of a flamingo is ____ (pink).
sentences.why: Pink is rosa in German — from the rose. (German pink exists but is the loud, neon pink.)

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von einer Aubergine ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of an aubergine is ____ (purple).
sentences.why: Purple is lila — from lilac; violett also works.

sentences.sentence: Viele Farben zusammen (ein Regenbogen) sind ____.
sentences.english: Many colours together (a rainbow) are ____ (colourful).
sentences.why: bunt means 'colourful, multi-coloured' — many colours at once; no single English colour matches it.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Tomaten und Kirschen ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of tomatoes and cherries is ____ (red).
sentences.why: Tomatoes and cherries are rot — 'red', cousin of 'rouge'.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Zitronen ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of lemons is ____ (yellow).
sentences.why: Lemons are gelb — 'yellow', from the same old root as gold.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von kleinen Schweinen ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of little pigs is ____ (pink).
sentences.why: Piglets are rosa — soft pink, from the rose.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Lavendel ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of lavender is ____ (purple).
sentences.why: Lavender is lila — the word comes from lilac.

sentences.sentence: Ein Clown trägt viele Farben. Sein Kostüm ist ____.
sentences.english: A clown wears lots of colours. His costume is ____ (colourful).
sentences.why: Many colours at once = bunt — colourful.

sentences.sentence: Die Farbe von Kakao ist ____.
sentences.english: The colour of cocoa is ____ (brown).
sentences.why: Cocoa is braun — 'brown' in German clothing: au = ow.

help.intro: Numbers are the words you will say most often in a German-speaking country — prices at the till, platform numbers at the station, room numbers, your own age and phone number — and they are also the words most often misheard, because the German sounds are not the English ones. This exercise is pure sound: listen and repeat, from null to a price. Three sounds carry it: z is ts (zwei = 'tsvai', zwanzig = 'TSVAN-tsikh'), ei is 'eye' (drei, zwei), and the -ig at the end of the tens is a soft 'ikh', not 'ig'. Say each one three times, and say the price out loud the German way — euros, then cents.

tips.title: z = ts, ei = eye, -ig = ikh
tips.text: zwei 'tsvai', zehn 'tsayn', zwanzig 'TSVAN-tsikh', dreißig 'DRY-ssikh'. The ts is the sound at the end of English 'cats'.

examples.de: zwei, zehn, zwölf, zwanzig
examples.en: tsvai, tsayn, tsvölf, TSVAN-tsikh

examples.de: drei, dreizehn, dreißig
examples.en: dry, DRY-tsayn, DRY-ssikh

check.q: How does vierzig end?
check.why: z is always ts, and -ig at the end is a soft “ikh”: FEER-tsikh.

tips.title: Prices: euros, then cents
tips.text: 3,50 € is 'drei Euro fünfzig'. No word for the comma, and Euro never takes an s.

examples.de: Das macht drei Euro fünfzig.
examples.en: That's 3.50 €.

examples.de: Ein Kaffee kostet zwei Euro zwanzig.
examples.en: A coffee costs 2.20 €.

check.q: Which is the natural way to say 4,80 €?
check.why: Euros first, then cents, with no word for the comma — and Euro never takes an s.

tips.title: Stress the first part
tips.text: SIEBzehn, VIERzig, EINundzwanzig. In compound numbers the very first syllable carries the weight; the rest is quick.

examples.de: einundzwanzig, siebenundvierzig
examples.en: EIN-und-tsvantsikh, SIE-ben-und-feertsikh

examples.de: SIEBzehn, VIERzig
examples.en: SEEB-tsayn, FEER-tsikh

check.q: Where does the stress go in neunzehn?
check.why: In numbers the first part carries the weight and the rest is quick: NEUNzehn, like SIEBzehn.

remember: Say your own phone number and age in German every day until they are automatic.
cats → zwei: the ts at the end of cats is the z at the start of every German number.
help.exam: A1 Sprechen: after your introduction the examiner asks you to spell a word and say a number — usually your phone number or postcode.
help.hook: Prices, platforms, phone numbers — numbers are what you'll say most, and three sounds make them sound truly German.
